newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside rises on NW Shelf expansion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside rises on NW Shelf expansion.

text.p: The shares of oil and gas company Woodside Petroleum Ltd rose after the company said on Thursday partners in the the North-West Shelf liquified natural gas project had agreed to a A$6.0 billion expansion.
At 11.35 a.m. (0135 GMT), Woodside shares were five cents firmer at A$8.80 on turnover of 172,982 shares.
Before the announcement of the expansion Woodside shares were trading 10 cents weaker at A$8.70.
"The rise is related to the expansion. The stock has gone up against the trend and there are not many sellers around which is a good sign for the stock," a Sydney dealer said.
Woodside earlier said the A$6 billion expansion would add about seven million tonnes per annum to the existing sales capacity of about 7.5 million tonnes per annum.

Woodside is an equal 16.66 percent shareholder in the project along with BHP Petroleum (North West Shelf) Pty Ltd, BP Developments Australia Ltd, Chevron Asiatic Ltd, Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd, and Japan Australia LNG (MIMI) Pty Ltd.
The shares of BHP, whose fortunes are not so closely linked to the gas project, were up 10 cents at A$17.32.
